intro: If you're looking for a place to spend a night near U-Tapao Airport before an early flight or after a late landing, without paying a fortune or dealing with the buzz of Pattaya, The Moonlight Resort is a little resort in Phla Subdistrict, Ban Chang District, that's likely to be just what you're after · It's a shady garden-style stay with only 15 rooms, a quiet and restful feel, spacious rooms with private balconies, a flower garden, a shaded sala to lounge in, free parking, and it's just a few minutes' drive from Phla Beach · Prices start at around THB 1,000/night · It scores about 7.7 from real reviews on Booking.com and Trip.com

body.html: Who The Moonlight Resort is for — to put it as simply as possible, The Moonlight Resort is a place for people who want "quiet and value" more than luxury amenities · It's not a beachfront resort with an infinity pool and a breakfast buffet, and it's not a hotel in central Pattaya where entertainment is right outside the door · It's a small garden resort of just 15 rooms tucked away in Phla Subdistrict, Ban Chang District, an area that's far quieter than Pattaya and close to U-Tapao-Rayong-Pattaya International Airport (UTP) · Real reviews point to the same kinds of guests: travelers with an early-morning flight or a late landing who want to stay near the airport for a night, road-trippers exploring the east coast who need a quiet stopover on the way to Rayong, families or couples who want to escape the bustle for a peaceful break, and budget travelers who want a clean, spacious room for a little over a thousand baht · On the flip side, if you're after nightlife, restaurants within walking distance, or big-hotel amenities, this may not be the answer, and the reviews say plainly that there's almost nothing in the way of entertainment or shops to stroll to in the evening around here · The draw here is the shady garden setting, the cleanliness, the privacy and the affordable price, rather than a stay you book for a full sweep of amenities

Location and getting around — the number-one strength of The Moonlight Resort is its location close to U-Tapao-Rayong-Pattaya International Airport (UTP), a growing airport serving both domestic flights and some international routes · The property lists the airport as about 14 km away, or roughly a 16-minute drive, while some sources measure the route as shorter depending on the way you go · Either way, it's close enough to be a comfortable base before a flight or after landing · The property offers airport transfers for an extra charge (some reviewers mention around 300 baht), which is handy for those not driving themselves · Beyond the airport, Phla Beach, Ban Chang's quiet stretch of coast, is only about a 5-minute drive away, ideal for anyone who wants an unhurried walk by the sea · Golf courses in the area, such as Eastern Star and Emerald Golf Course, aren't far either, which makes this a pick for golfers playing around Ban Chang and Rayong · Central Pattaya lies to the northwest, about a 30-40 minute drive, so it suits people who use this as a quiet base and drive into town occasionally rather than those staying mainly to explore Pattaya · One important note is that a location like this nearly requires a car — your own, a rental or a ride-hail — because there are no shops or public transport within easy walking distance the way there would be in town

"Booked it to stay before an early flight out of U-Tapao, and it turned out to be more than worth the price. The room was huge, clean, the garden lovely and quiet — and the owner was kind and spoke English, so no stress with communication. Next time we pass through this way we'll stay again."

Room types and decor — The Moonlight Resort is a small property with around 15 rooms, and the main room type found on booking platforms is the Economy Double Room, with one large bed, a window and a non-smoking policy · The point reviews agree on most is that the rooms are more spacious than you'd expect for the price — many people are surprised by how much space they get for what they pay · The decor is simple and clean, not luxurious but genuinely usable · In-room amenities cover everything you need for a comfortable stay: air conditioning, a fridge, cable TV, an en-suite bathroom with a shower and toiletries, and a guest favorite, a private balcony where you can sit, catch the breeze and look out over the garden · Some foreign reviewers praise the neatly tiled bathroom and the overall cleanliness as very well done, "spotless" even · That said, to be straight about it, a few reviews have minor gripes — the blanket is a bit thin, almost like a large bath towel, and bathroom items such as a bar of soap aren't always provided · These are small details you'll find in budget stays, and they don't dent the overall satisfaction of most guests · If you get cold easily, it's worth bringing a light throw of your own or asking for an extra blanket

Facilities and the garden setting — you need to understand first that The Moonlight Resort is a small resort, so there's no swimming pool, gym or spa like at a big hotel · Anyone coming specifically for a pool should skip this and choose a resort with one outright · But what it does have, and what's genuinely charming, is the shady garden setting · The grounds are laid out as a flower garden, with large trees for shade and a shaded sala that's perfect for a morning coffee or an evening wind-down · Several reviews mention the "neatly kept, pretty flower garden" and the especially quiet surroundings as something that genuinely helps you relax · Facilities on hand include free private parking on site, which matters a lot for a location where you need a car, an electric vehicle (EV) charging point that's uncommon at this price, free Wi-Fi in the common areas, a shared kitchen for preparing your own food, a picnic area and barbecue space, plus bicycle rental for getting around · The daily housekeeping and towel changes also earn praise for their attentiveness · Overall the facilities here are enough for a simple stay focused on cleanliness and privacy, rather than a wide range of activities

Food and nearby eats — food is a point that needs to be spelled out clearly, because the information varies from platform to platform · Some booking sources state the property has no breakfast service, while some TripAdvisor reviews recount getting a simple breakfast such as eggs in a pan, two kinds of sausage, and tea or coffee · This difference may come down to the time of year, the package booked, or talking to the owner directly · The safest advice is to confirm breakfast when you book or before check-in so you don't set the wrong expectation · Since the property has a shared kitchen and barbecue area, many people choose to buy ingredients and cook for themselves or grill in the garden setting, which fits the quiet style of staying here · For main meals, foreign reviewers mention a genuine Thai restaurant across the road as convenient and tasty · Beyond that, Phla Subdistrict and the town of Ban Chang have made-to-order eateries, seafood restaurants and cafes scattered about, a short drive away · In short, food isn't a highlight here, but it's not a hardship either — with a car you'll find plenty to eat, and if you like cooking you can make full use of the shared kitchen and barbecue area

Service and the owner — for a small property like this, service is tied directly to the owner and a handful of staff, which turns out to be one of The Moonlight Resort's strengths · Real reviews speak about the owner and staff positively and consistently, using words like "very friendly," "attentive" and "flexible and helpful" · A point that puts foreign travelers especially at ease is that the team speaks English, so sorting out check-in, airport transfers, or asking about where to eat and what to see goes smoothly · There's 24-hour reception, check-in and check-out are personal, and there are useful extra services like airport transfers, car rental and bicycle rental · It's this "staying at a friend's house" or warm guesthouse feeling that leaves many guests impressed beyond the price they paid · One thing to bear in mind is that, because it's a small property with few staff, you may need to arrange a late check-in or transfer in advance at certain times to keep everything running smoothly

Voices from real reviews (praise and gripes) — gathered from Booking.com, Trip.com and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent, even though the number of reviews is still small (a small, fairly new property) · On the praise side: very clean rooms that are bigger than expected, a quiet garden setting that genuinely helps you relax, strong value for money, a friendly owner and team who speak English, a location near U-Tapao Airport that's handy for connections or early flights, and proximity to Phla Beach and the Thai restaurant across the road · On the watch-out side: the most-mentioned point is that the location is so quiet there's almost nothing to do in the evening — no nightlife, shops or entertainment within walking distance, and anyone who likes a lively scene might feel lonely · Next come the small in-room details like the thin blanket and bathroom items that are sometimes incomplete, the fact there's no swimming pool or big-resort amenities, and the need for a car since getting around on foot isn't practical · Almost all of these gripes are about "setting the right expectations" rather than serious flaws — if you come because you want quiet and a light price, these things turn out to be pluses

"Very clean, lovely owner, the garden pretty, quiet and genuinely restful · The only downside is that it's very quiet at night with nothing to do, so you have to drive out to find food. Anyone without a car might find it a bit of a hassle."

Price comparison and value — The Moonlight Resort's prices are clearly in the budget bracket, with the Economy Double starting at around THB 1,000/night (lower during some promotions) and edging up a little over long weekends or holidays · Compared with the usual hotels near U-Tapao Airport or stays in central Pattaya that tend to start higher, this place feels very good value in terms of space and cleanliness for the price · What makes it genuinely worthwhile is that you get a spacious, clean room with a balcony, set in a quiet garden, with free parking, for a price that's sometimes cheaper than a tiny room in town · Of course, you trade that for no swimming pool, no guaranteed breakfast, and a location where you need a car · So the value here depends on what you put a premium on — if you value quiet, cleanliness and a light budget, this place is great value · But if you measure value by the number of amenities or how easy it is to get out and explore on foot, you may feel something is still missing · For a one-night transit stay near the airport, or a quiet break, this price feels like money well spent

Things to know before you book — there are several things that help the stay go more smoothly · One, plan your transport, because this location nearly requires your own car, a rental or a transfer service — if you don't have a car, book the airport transfer in advance (an extra charge of around 300 baht according to reviews) · Two, confirm breakfast before booking, since the information varies by source — some say there is none, some reviews say there's a simple one · Three, if you get cold easily, bring a light throw of your own or ask for an extra blanket, as some reviews note the blanket is rather thin · Four, set the right expectation that there's no swimming pool and no nightlife here — come for quiet and rest, not entertainment · Five, give a clear check-in time in advance, especially if you arrive late or your flight lands late, because it's a small property with few staff and arranging ahead keeps everything smooth · Six, there's an EV charging point on site, a plus for anyone driving an electric car around the east coast

The verdict — from all the real reviews, The Moonlight Resort is best suited to people who want a budget stay near U-Tapao Airport with quiet surroundings and clean, spacious rooms · The location near the airport and Phla Beach, the shady garden, a friendly owner who speaks English, free parking and prices a little over a thousand baht make it a solid choice for a transit stay or a quiet break · If you're looking for a swimming pool, a breakfast buffet, nightlife or a location you can explore on foot, this isn't the answer, and you should consider a hotel in central Pattaya or a beachfront resort with fuller amenities instead · But for those who understand what they're booking — a small, quiet garden resort with a light price, close to the airport — The Moonlight Resort meets that need for more than its price suggests, which is why many guests say they'd stay again if they pass through Ban Chang

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — The Moonlight Resort, Ban Chang

faq.q: Where is The Moonlight Resort, and how close is it to U-Tapao Airport?
faq.a: The property is in Phla Subdistrict, Ban Chang District, near the Chonburi-Rayong border · It's about 14 km, or a 16-minute drive, from U-Tapao-Rayong-Pattaya International Airport (UTP), and only about a 5-minute drive from Phla Beach · Airport transfers are available (for an extra charge), making it ideal for early flights or late landings

faq.q: What does The Moonlight Resort start at, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 1,000/night for the Economy Double Room, with a large bed and a private balcony · It's a small property with around 15 rooms, sometimes lower during promotions and edging up a little over long weekends · It sits in the budget bracket and offers good value in terms of space and cleanliness for the price

faq.q: Does The Moonlight Resort have a swimming pool and breakfast?
faq.a: There's no swimming pool, as it's a small garden resort focused on quiet · As for breakfast, the information varies by source — some platforms say there is none, while some reviews recount a simple breakfast — so it's best to confirm with the property before booking · There's a shared kitchen and barbecue area for cooking your own food

faq.q: Who is The Moonlight Resort for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for people who want a budget stay near U-Tapao Airport, road-trippers on the east coast looking for a quiet stopover, golfers around Ban Chang-Rayong, and couples or families wanting a peaceful break · If you're after nightlife, restaurants within walking distance, or big-hotel amenities, central Pattaya may suit you better

faq.q: Do you need a car to stay at The Moonlight Resort?
faq.a: Nearly · The Phla Subdistrict location is quiet with no public transport nearby, so walking to restaurants or the beach isn't practical · Having your own car or a rental is easiest (free parking on site) · If you don't have a car, book the property's airport transfer in advance and plan for ride-hailing when you head out to eat

faq.q: What are the atmosphere and cleanliness at The Moonlight Resort like?
faq.a: Real reviews agree that the rooms are very clean and bigger than expected, with a private balcony · The grounds are laid out as a shady flower garden with a lounging sala, quiet and private, which helps you relax · The owner and team are friendly and speak English · One small note is that the blanket is rather thin and bathroom items are sometimes incomplete
